name: Select
statusNote: Stable in use; alpha is Primer's label. It is a styled native <select>, so the open list is the platform's, not Primer's.
summary: A single choice from a short fixed list, drawn as TextInput's well with an up-down arrow and opening the platform's native option list. Choose it for plain-text options in a form; choose ActionMenu or SelectPanel for rich items, filtering or multiple selection.

inputs.name: options
inputs.description: Select.Option children, each a value and a plain-text label, optionally grouped under Select.OptGroup labels; options may be disabled.

inputs.name: value
inputs.description: The chosen option's value. Controlled when given; otherwise defaultValue seeds it.

inputs.name: placeholder
inputs.description: Text shown as a first option with an empty value. When required it is disabled and hidden from the list, so it can only show before a choice.

inputs.name: validationStatus
inputs.description: Border colour; error also sets aria-invalid.

inputs.name: required
inputs.description: A choice other than the placeholder is needed to submit.

inputs.name: onChange
inputs.description: Called with the new value when the user picks an option.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: TextInput's well: 1px --control-borderColor-rest border, medium radius, --bgColor-default fill, --shadow-inset; clips its content and positions the arrow.

anatomy.name: Selected label
anatomy.description: The chosen option's label (or the placeholder) on one line in the container's text colour, inset 12px each side.

anatomy.name: Arrow indicator
anatomy.description: A 16px up-and-down double triangle in currentColor, 4px from the end edge, vertically centred, ignoring the pointer (Select.tsx:26 gives the path).

anatomy.name: Option list
anatomy.description: The platform's native popup list of options and group headings; Primer does not style it.

variants.description: 28px minimum height, 3px block padding, small body text.

layout.text: The container is TextInput's with no visuals and no action: an inline row at least 32px tall (28px small, 40px fixed at large) whose select fills the full width and height.

The label is inset 12px from both edges (the no-visuals padding), so the 16px arrow at 4px from the end overlaps the last 8px of the label's box; long labels run under the arrow before they are clipped.
The arrow is absolutely positioned in the container: 4px from the end, centred vertically, not hit-testable, so presses on it reach the select.

The select carries a 1px margin on top, bottom and start (a Firefox workaround that keeps an inset focus shadow visible); it is 100% wide, so it overflows the container by 1px at the end and is clipped.
Width hugs the native select's intrinsic width, which is the widest option's label plus padding, unless block.

states.text: Rest: --bgColor-default fill, --control-borderColor-rest border, --shadow-inset, pointer cursor. The select's own background inherits the container's, and its corners follow the container's radius.
While the select has focus, by pointer or keyboard, the border turns --borderColor-accent-emphasis with a 2px outline of the same colour at offset -1px. No hover state.
Border --borderColor-danger-emphasis; focused, the border and outline turn --control-borderColor-danger.

Text and arrow --fgColor-disabled, fill --control-bgColor-disabled, border --control-borderColor-disabled, no shadow, not-allowed cursor. The select's own background turns transparent so a translucent disabled fill is not painted twice.
Opening shows the platform's option list; the field keeps its focused look while it is open.

behaviour.text: A press or the keyboard opens the native list; choosing an option closes it, shows its label and calls onChange.

With a placeholder, a first option with an empty value and the placeholder text precedes the options. If required, that option is disabled and hidden, so once a real option is chosen the placeholder cannot be chosen again.
Group headings (Select.OptGroup) label runs of options and are not selectable.

keyboard: Space, Enter or Alt+Down opens the list (per platform); Up and Down move the choice, on some platforms without opening.
Typing a letter jumps to the next option starting with it.
Escape closes the list without changing the choice.
semantics: aria-invalid is always set: true for error, false otherwise.
required is the native attribute; the arrow is aria-hidden.

notes.text: The open list, its positioning, scrolling, typeahead, keyboard model and option rendering are the browser's and the OS's (on macOS a native menu over the field, on mobile a picker sheet). A native build must provide the popup itself, conventionally an overlay list anchored to the field with the chosen option marked, or delegate to a platform menu.
appearance: none removes the platform's own arrow and chrome; the drawn arrow is an SVG over the field. Long labels are clipped by the field, not ellipsised.
Select's intrinsic width is the widest option, not the chosen one, so the field does not change width as the choice changes. A native build measures every option label to size it.

defaultValue falls back to the placeholder text, which matches no option (the placeholder's value is the empty string); which option then shows first is left to React's and the browser's fallback, and with a required, disabled placeholder that can be the first real option. A native build shows the placeholder whenever the value is empty.
Select.docs.json lists a contrast prop, but SelectProps omits contrast and Select never passes it to the wrapper; there is no contrast Select.
Under forced colours the arrow fills FieldText, GrayText when disabled; Firefox keeps a disabled select's background with -moz-combobox.
The arrow's colour is currentColor of the container, so it follows the text colour: --fgColor-default at rest, --fgColor-disabled when disabled. It is not --fgColor-muted like TextInput's visuals.
